We would like to know how well our optimized GCN algorithm, which we call Mod-GCN , performs on average for Erdős-Rényi graphs of many different orders and sizes. Figure 2 , in orange, shows the result of running Mod-GCN on 100 100 different Erdős-Rényi graphs for all n ∈ { 10 , 20 , … , 200 } n\in\{10,20,\dots,200\} and d ∈ { 2 , 4 , … , 20 } d\in\{2,4,\dots,20\} , then recording the average loss and an approximate 95% confidence interval for the true mean. One striking result is that the average loss is almost perfectly linear in n n for most d d and sufficiently large n n . This justifies our decision to keep n = 200 n=200 fixed in the previous experiment, since it suggests that an improvement for any particular n n is an improvement for all n n .
